s: High-traffic entries, courtyards, and shared-use areas tend to do best with denser turf and a stable install that prevents shifting at seams. If the install is on a rooftop deck or elevated surface, weight and drainage become bigger factors, along with how you will handle transitions at doors, drains, and edges. For larger commercial layouts, planning roll placement up front is key so you can reduce seams, keep traffic lanes on the most consistent sections, and avoid piecing together small cuts in prominent areas. Buying used turf online can feel a little opaque, especially when inventory changes fast and specs are not always presented the same way.
